answer: Convex pulse-lease pricing: agents buy short-lived execution pulses; each pulse costs base × exp(k × c), where c is the share of epoch pulses from the buyer’s inferred cluster (shared funding/timing/call graph). A fresh cluster starts cheap, but as a Sybil swarm ramps, its marginal pulse price climbs an exponential ledge; N fakes cost superlinearly. Attackers must split across a vine of independent clusters, paying separate funding, infrastructure, and coordination overhead.
